full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1-6 to show cause as to why the judgment and order of affordance dated 22.042004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. Bhola in Miscellaneous Appeal No.31 of 1994 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor of the present opposite party No.1-6 one Faizunnessa as plaintiff tiled the original Title Suit No.49 of 1987 in the court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge. Bhola against the present petitioners for partition. The plaintiffs on 25.08.1987 filed an application under Order 39, Rule I read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an order of temporary injunction against the defendants. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge after hearing the said application passed an order of status-quo on 25.08.1987 directing the parties to maintain status-quo with a notice to show cause upon the defendants as to why the temporary injunction should not be granted. The present petitioner No.1 on 09.09.1987 received the said notice and accordingly submitted written objection. The order of status-quo was not extended further and eventually the application for temporary injunction was not heard. On 30.01.1988 the plaintiff filed an application under Order 39, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure upon which a Miscellaneous case being No.7 of 1988 was started. In the said Miscellaneous case the plaintiff alleged that during pendency of the order of status-quo the present petitioners along with others on 21.01.1988 forcibly entered into the schedule land and made obstruction in cultivation and also damaged the standing crops ("Mugdal") of 128 decimals of land causing damage of Tk.5,000/-. The plaintiff also lodged a G.D. entry in the respective Police Station and the Police authority served notice under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but ultimately all are in vain. The present petitioners after getting notice of the violation Miscellaneous case filed written objection and denied all the allegations raised against them contending inter-alia that the statement made in the application under order 39, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure is false, fabricated and the defendant-petitioners never violated the order of status-quo. The original Title Suit No.49 of 1987 was decreed on 04.11.1993 and being aggrieved the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.47 of 1994 in the court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was admitted for hearing by the said court and the learned District Judge called for the lower court's record and transmitted the case to the court of learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Advocate for the defendants talked to the defendants that the hearing of the violation miscellaneous case might not be held by the court and accordingly no step was taken by the defendants who are the opposite parties to the violation miscellaneous case. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bhola on 02.07.1994 behind the back of the present petitioners after examining one witness passed an ex-parte judgment and order of conviction of six months civil imprisonment. 

 3. Being aggrieved the present petitioners as appellants preferred a Miscellaneous Appeal No.31 of 1994 in the court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Bhola and the learned lower appellate court by the impugned judgment and order dated 22.04.2004 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge. 

 6. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during passing the judgment and order committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the ad-interim order of status-quo was passed on 25.08.1987 and the application for injunction was filed on 21.08.1987. In fact on 21.08.1987 there was no order of status-quo against the petitioners. The trial court passed an order of civil imprisonment on 02.07.1994 but the fact remains that on the date of alleged violation of the order of status-quo there was no order of status-quo or injunction whatsoever against the present petitioners. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge is totally misconceived in this regard and by non-application of mind he passed the ex-parte order on 02.07.1994 and subsequently the lower appellate court without entering into the facts of the case being guided by surmise and conjecture upheld the order of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order dated 22.04.2004. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court was without jurisdiction to pass any order on 02.07.1994 inasmuch as against the judgment and decree of the original Title Suit 49 of 1987 a Title Appeal was pending wherein the original record was called for and the order was communicated to the court of learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bhola. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the violation Miscellaneous case since is quasi criminal in nature the trial court had incumbent duty to bring charge in the form of issues mentioning the date of occurrence, time of occurrence and manner of occurrence and in this context the learned counsel referred some decisions of this court reported in 12 BLD 544, 39 DLR 262, 1987 BLD 73, 13 BLD 532. 

 7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court committed no illegality in passing the order of civil imprisonment and the order of affordance respectively. The learned Advocate further submits that on 25.08.1987 the learned trial court in Title Suit No.49 of 1987 passed an order of status-quo and after that order following date was fixed on 20.09.1987 and had there been no such extension order of status-quo, the learned courts below might not have been passed the order of imprisonment. The learned Advocate also submits that the written objection which was filed in the violation Miscellaneous case does not disclose that on 21.01.1988 there was no order of status-quo_ or injunction against the defendants. The learned Advocate lastly submits that both the courts below after perusal of the connected papers and deposition of the petitioner No. I (ka) of the violation Miscellaneous case No.7 of 1988 being satisfied passed the order which is lawful and is not liable to be interfered with. 

 8. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, connected papers, deposition of the witness Md. Hanif Mia and the concerned application for violation of the courts order along with the written objection filed against that. 

 9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the plaintiff to the suit on 20.08.1987 filed an application for temporary injunction against the defendants of the original partition suit being No.49 of 1987. On that application the learned trial court passed an order of status-quo vide order No.4 on 25.08,1987 until) the reply of show cause notice from the side of the defendants. The defendants subsequently appeared after getting show cause notice and submitted written objection. The allegation of violation was raised on the date of occurrence i.e. on 21.01.1988 but prior to that the defendants submitted their written objection. No where it is noticed that the ad-interim order of status-quo was extended after 25.08.1987. The petitioner 1(ka) of the violation Miscellaneous case No.7 of 1988 in his testimony admits that after service of notice the defendants appeared and submitted written objection. Subsequent to that on 21.01.1988 violating the order of status-quo they have damaged the crops valued Tk.5,000/-. The learned lower appellate court without entering into the case record relied upon the Miscellaneous petition and the order of civil imprisonment which was passed ex-parte by the learned trial court vide order No.153 dated 02.07.1994, 

 10. In a case or proceedings for violation of injunction it is the incumbent duty upon the court to bring charge in the form of points for determination disclosing all material particulars of the allegation i.e. the date of occurrence, time of occurrence and manner of occurrence since the case is of quasi criminal in nature. The proposition of law has imposed a mandatory duty upon the trial court to dispose of the matter in accordance with the direction but apparently the learned trial court passed an order of civil imprisonment without compliance of that, which is evasive in nature and not speaking and well reasoned. The learned appellate court subsequently ignoring the provisions of law and facts of the case affirmed the order of the trial court illegally which deserve interference of this court. 

 11. In the result, the Rule having much substance is made absolute without any order as to costs. The judgment and order of affirmance dated 22.04.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bhola in Miscellaneous Appeal No.31 of 1994 is hereby set aside.
